images.title: One fifth or one ninth
images.purpose: Show that one fifth of a roti is greater than one ninth of the same roti, because more sharers give a smaller fractional unit.
images.composition: Two equal round rotis stacked one above the other on the left, and on the right one large overlay of the two coloured pieces, with wide space between.
images.exact_structure: Left top: one round roti cut by straight lines from the centre into 5 equal pieces, one piece filled teal #0072B2. Left bottom: one round roti of exactly the same size cut from the centre into 9 equal pieces, one piece filled amber #E69F00. Right: the teal piece with the amber piece laid on top of it, tips together and one straight edge lined up, the amber piece covering only part of the teal piece. Exactly 2 rotis, 2 coloured pieces, 1 overlay.

images.takeaway: More sharers of the same whole means a smaller fractional unit, so 1/5 > 1/9.
images.description: A roti cut into 5 equal pieces and a same-size roti cut into 9 equal pieces; the 1/9 piece laid on the 1/5 piece covers only part of it, showing 1/5 > 1/9.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the part of the teal piece the amber piece does not cover and say which unit is greater.

image_decisions.why: Laying one ninth on one fifth of the same roti makes the comparison visible in one look.
